s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually developing skin lesion with verrucous appearance and soft-tissue mass
salient_findings: Slightly reddish verrucous plaque on the right temple
Translucent papules and plaques with surface hemorrhagic crust
Papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia and neoplastic infiltration of small round blue cells
key_facts: Asymptomatic skin lesion on the right temple
Lesion gradually developed over 8 months
No associated fevers, weight loss, or night sweats
Lesion is nontender with no purulent discharge
No hepatosplenomegaly or superficial lymphadenopathy
Laboratory tests showed no abnormalities
Imaging studies revealed skin thickening and a soft-tissue mass in the right frontotemporal region
Histopathology showed papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia and neoplastic infiltration
Tumor cells are positive for MyoD1, myogenin, vimentin, and desmin

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Positive for MyoD1, myogenin, vimentin, and desmin, consistent with rhabdomyosarcoma

shortlist.label: Verrucous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Verrucous appearance and gradual development of the skin lesion

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Soft-tissue mass and skin thickening in the right frontotemporal region

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Positive for vimentin and desmin, with possible smooth muscle origin

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia and neoplastic infiltration, with possible squamous origin

raw.rationale: The tumor cells are positive for MyoD1, myogenin, vimentin, and desmin, which are markers for muscle differentiation, consistent with rhabdomyosarcoma. The histopathology also shows small round blue cells with alternating areas of dense and loose cellularity, a characteristic feature of rhabdomyosarcoma.

rejected.label: Verrucous carcinoma
rejected.why: While the lesion has a verrucous appearance, the immunohistochemistry results do not support a diagnosis of verrucous carcinoma, which is typically positive for cytokeratins.

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: The histopathology and immunohistochemistry results do not match the typical features of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, which is usually positive for CD34 and negative for muscle markers.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: The tumor cells are not positive for smooth muscle markers, and the histopathology does not show the typical features of leiomyosarcoma, which is usually composed of spindle cells with a fascicular growth pattern.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The immunohistochemistry results do not support a diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma, which is typically positive for cytokeratins and negative for muscle markers.
